title: Save six primitives in one signed JP8 continuation (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Finite local circuit certificate with a scoped substitution proof, produced by Nick Petalas. One signed continuation in the historical PR626 JP8 forward fragment `[19709,19713)` preserves its arbitrary-input map, target order and private-work clearing while saving six real-component primitives per complex application.

```diff
- PR811: two cleared blocks, 17 primitives per real component
+ signed continuation: one merged block, 14 primitives per real component
```

At the join, the established work value is `3s/2`. Replace `clear w; clear w; w += s; halve w` with `w -= s`. All later operations are identical. No extra register, child, frame change or source access is omitted. The recursive moment remains unchanged, and no new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Ryan Haines / [PR811](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/811) supplies the source and positive-read compiler; [PR830](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/830) supplies transposition context. AmazedBot / [PR860](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/860) already studies the signed-continuation mechanism on CK. The new contribution is this explicit JP8 application, not a new general shift/add method. The source retains the Kothe, Boukhalfa, icekylinx, Cox, ellipsi2, Thakrar and native/compiler lineage. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19370136).

## Evidence

At head `d3fbef0a2ac05fbf32f17d272cc76c95cc057dbf`, warning-strict CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized verification pass with identical generated hash-bound receipts. The complete six-input rational matrix matches the direct specification. A separate integer interpreter passes all 15,625 grid inputs per program. Seven semantic controls reject. Source authentication and metadata, syntax/whitespace, registered replay and committed-byte/source-history checks pass locally. No predecessor scientific replay or whole-program recount is performed.

Direct normal/optimized checks took 0.1069 / 0.1103 seconds; the registered command took 0.5825 seconds. These are local replay-deadline measurements, not a performance claim. Every registered check ran locally.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/jp8-signed-continuation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/jp8-signed-continuation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/jp8-signed-continuation
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/jp8-signed-continuation --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 path may substitute. Expected marker: `PASS_JP8_SIGNED_CONTINUATION`.

## Limitations

This is an explicitly changed scalar-to-moment card scope and a historical side result. Exact prefix cancellation does not transfer the predecessor's cancellation-free rounding budget. No superiority to every standalone compiler or additive composition with PR696/723/882/999/1223 is claimed. Backward application, complete native/physical integration, whole-word rounded precision, tape/storage/stock, compiler and outer admission remain unrun or unresolved. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human review or formal proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

Can one signed continuation fit a current complete caller and its fully recomputed rounded prefix budget? First extract one source-compatible private-work boundary, then charge conversion and cleanup and derive cancellation-free error bounds. Current source binding, physical integration and a complete consumer bill are the blockers. No follow-up is reserved.

## Related open work

- [PR815](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/815) studies historical PR626/741 frame assignment and paid-profile optimality, including JP8. This changes a local scalar implementation and computes no competing frame optimum or kappa.
- [PR729](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/729) audits helper-frame lifetime coverage in the historical PR626 providers. This preserves the four full-frame events and makes no new lifetime-audit claim.

The completion refresh inspected the twelve other open contributions created after the advance claim: #6555, #6557, #6558, #6559, #6560, #6561, #6562, #6563, #6564, #6565, #6566 and #6567. None studies this historical JP8 fragment or reports a competing value for its local primitive bill. No additional computation rechecked another contribution.

The completed checks were read once; run metadata confirms successful completion at the matching head. Hosted replay executes the registered normal and optimized checks. All registered commands and publication integrity checks also passed locally. CI certifies execution of the bounded checks and source metadata; independent mathematical and formal proof-kernel acceptance remain unclaimed.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Six new files under `research/jp8-signed-continuation/`; no shared implementation, selected record or frozen predecessor is changed.
